summary: Run playbooks with --vault-id user@file or @prompt instead of -k. Check a decrypted value with the debug module (stripping ansible_connection first). Rotate the vault password with ansible-vault rekey.
questions: How do I run a playbook that uses vaulted variables?
How do I view a decrypted vault variable?
How do I change my vault password?
Can old copies be decrypted after rekeying?

answer_card.title: Run with vault and rekey
answer_card.answer_md:
```console
ansible-playbook -i inventory --vault-id my_user@~/my-ansible-vault-pw-file first_playbook.yml
ansible-playbook -i inventory --vault-id my_user@prompt first_playbook.yml
```
View a value (remove `ansible_connection` from the file first so it doesn't apply to localhost):
```console
grep -v ansible_connection vyos.yml > vyos_no_connection.yml
ansible localhost -m debug -a var="ansible_password" -e "@vyos_no_connection.yml" --ask-vault-pass
```
Change password: `ansible-vault rekey myfile`. Copies still encrypted with the old password remain decryptable with it.
